properties.name: rustfmt reflowed the file after the first baseline was taken; behaviour is unchanged and all three tests still pass. NO DESIGN MEANING. Caught by the CI design-coherence gate, not by me — and it is the fourth instance of the same self-inflicted error: HASHING BEFORE THE LAST EDIT. The specific trap here is new and worth naming: `cargo fmt --check` is a CI gate, so running fmt is a REQUIRED step that happens AFTER the work looks finished, which puts a file mutation after the natural moment to hash. The rule that actually holds is hash last, after fmt, immediately before the export.
